rows.question: What is the exposure dial's rule?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The dial is simple: it's OPEN, meaning buying is allowed, only when Bitcoin's daily close is above both its 50-day and its 200-day average. Otherwise it's CLOSED, with no new buys and cash is the position. Right now it's open: Bitcoin closed yesterday at about 81,900, above the 50-day at about 80,600 and the 200-day at about 72,600. That's only about 1.6% of cushion over the 50-day, so one close under it flips the dial.

rows.question: Which daily rule has a measured edge, and in which market state?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Only one daily rule has a measured edge: the short dip trade (H07). It works on tier-A coins, the big liquid ones, and only while the exposure dial is closed. That means Bitcoin is below its 50-day or 200-day average. In that state it beat random by about 10% a trade in 2018-2023 and about 7% a trade in 2024 to mid-2026, after costs. We expect about 6% a trade over random going forward. Today the dial is OPEN, so we're outside that cell, and every other daily rule has no measured edge. Zone touches are the worst so far, averaging about -14% on open tier-A paper trades and -13% on

rows.question: How many coins do you watch live across the market?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We watch about 393 coins live: every coin trading against USDT on Binance, with each rule run on every one. Tier A is the big coins, tier B is mid-size, and tier C is small coins that we watch but never judge. Ten of them, the lab coins, also get the 15-minute Explorer scan. Want the tier breakdown and how healthy the feed is?

rows.question: What did review 27 find about stops on dip buys?
need: no stop|without a stop|time exit|exit by time|time only
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Review 27 found that the short dip trade does best with no stop and a 10-day time exit. With a stop it earned about half a percent a trade in 2018-23 and 0.4% in 2024-26. With no stop it earned about 6.5% and 2.4% in those same periods. A tight 3% stop was hit in 70 to 85% of trades, so it cut winners off. The edge is measured in one cell only: big tier-A coins while the exposure dial is closed. The dial is open today, so there's no measured edge right now. Want me to walk through review 29, which re-checked that cell on all the Binance pairs? Just say yes.

rows.question: What is the benchmark every strategy must beat?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The benchmark is the Bitcoin 50-day rule book, which we call GATE50. It holds coins only while Bitcoin closes above its 50-day average and sits in cash otherwise. Every strategy has to beat it after costs, and it's a tougher bar than buy-and-hold. The exposure dial (Bitcoin above both its 50-day and 200-day averages) beat it in both test periods, but GATE50 stays the hurdle. Want me to pull up how the books compare right now?

rows.question: Did tuning the deep-dip buy E6 in review 24 work?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. No, the tuning didn't work. Review 24 tested every variant of the deep-dip buy (E6), and none passed. They all lose money after costs in both periods, and none beats random in the confirmation test. The live Explorer agrees: its E6 trades keep closing at tiny losses or wins on the warning bell, and the book is down about 264 dollars overall. Want the variant numbers?

rows.question: What fee per side do we assume on NDAX?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We assume 0.20% per side on NDAX as the fee, plus the spread on top. For the 10 lab coins we use the measured spread. For coins outside the lab 10 we assume 0.40%. So a round trip costs at least 0.40% in fees alone, and that's why most short-term ideas lost: costs ate the edge.

rows.question: How much of the book does one setup trade risk in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. In the $500 book, each setup trade risks 0.5% of the book, which is about two and a half dollars if the stop is hit. No single trade can be more than 10% of the book, about fifty dollars in size. All open trades together can risk at most 6% of the book, about thirty dollars.

rows.question: What daily loss stops new buys in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. A 2% loss in one day stops new buys in the $500 book, about $10. I checked: no brake has fired, and the book isn't paused. It's worth about $488, down 2.3%, holding Bitcoin and Ethereum as its core. The other brakes are 4% in a week, four losses in a row, and a 15% fall from the high, which pauses it until you resume.

rows.question: What happens if the 500 dollar book falls 15% from its peak?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. If the $500 book falls 15% from its peak, it pauses. It buys nothing new until you resume it yourself. The automatic rules won't restart it. That's one of four brakes. The others are a 2% loss in a day, a 4% loss in a week, and four losing trades in a row. None has fired so far. The book is worth about 488 Canadian dollars, down about 2.3% since Oct 11, so the 15% brake is far off. The day and week brakes would most likely trip first. The book also isn't ready for real money: it has passed 2 of 10 graduation gates and has made no round-trip trades yet. Want me to walk through wha

rows.question: How many losing trades in a row pause buying?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Four losses in a row pause buying. That's one of the brakes on the $500 account book. The others are a 2% loss in a day, a 4% loss in a week, and a 15% fall from the high. Once any of them fires, buying stays paused until you resume it.

rows.question: What does the core sleeve of the 500 dollar book hold?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The core sleeve holds two coins, Bitcoin and Ethereum, both bought on Oct 11 when the exposure dial opened. Bitcoin is about 200 Canadian dollars paid, which is the 40% share. Ethereum is about 100 dollars, the 20% share. Both have slipped since the buys, so the book is worth about 488 dollars, down 2.3%, with about 199 dollars in cash. The dial is still open, so the core stays invested. Want me to go through the graduation gates? Just say yes.

rows.question: Which exchange is the 500 dollar book built for?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The $500 book is built for NDAX, in Canadian dollars. Its fills are checked against NDAX's bid and ask. It's paper only, so no exchange is connected and no real order can go out.

rows.question: How many trigger points does an Explorer setup give the brain now?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. An Explorer setup gives the brain zero trigger points now. That came from the repair-shop change that made the brain's trigger points follow the evidence. The Explorer's setups were rejected after costs, so they no longer wake the brain.

rows.question: What daily trading volume puts a coin in tier A?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. A coin is tier A when it trades more than $20 million a day. Tier B is $1 million to $20 million, and tier C is under $1 million. We watch tier C coins but never judge or trade them.

rows.question: What do you hold when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. When the dial is closed, we hold cash. The $500 account's core goes to cash, and the only thing allowed to buy is the short dip trade on big tier-A coins, with no stop and a 10-day exit. Right now the trend portfolio holds nothing either. It's all cash, about $1,849, and it's down about 7.6% since the start. Buy-and-hold is down about 12%.

rows.question: What is the H07 entry?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The short dip trade (H07) buys a coin when its 10-day RSI, a gauge of how stretched the price is, closes under 30 while the coin is still above its 200-day average. It exits when RSI is back over 40, or after 10 days. There's no stop, because review #18 found no-stop dips did far better than tight stops.

rows.question: What is Madhav's M1 setup?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. M1 is your capitulation-at-the-lows setup, modeled on your June 5 Solana buy: a sharp sell-off where many give up at once, and you buy near the low. History didn't back it on its own. In review #5 and #15 it did no better than a random day, so it only marks a place to look, not a reason to buy.

rows.question: How many coins are in the research lake?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The research lake holds 120 coins. That's the full research universe, with checked history back to 2017, dead coins included. Only the 10 lab coins are fully live, and we watch about 393 coins on Binance in the broader live feed. Want me to show the three tiers side by side?

rows.question: Is the hourly watch running?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. No, the hourly watch isn't running. You parked it on purpose on Oct 11, and the code is kept. Everything else is healthy, including the 15-minute Explorer, which last scanned 8 minutes ago. Hunter's book is frozen at 3 wins and 19 losses. Only the worker Mac, which provides NDAX spreads, keeps dropping offline.

rows.question: What will Bitcoin's price be on December 31, 2026?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you Bitcoin's price on December 31. Nobody can, and I won't invent a number. It's about 81,500 now, and I expect chop between roughly 80 and 85 thousand over the next few days, which says little about year-end.

rows.question: Will Ethereum beat Solana next month?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't call that one, and I won't pretend to. We have no tested rule that picks a winner between two coins a month out. Right now neither looks like a leader. Ethereum is down about four percent this week and Solana about two and a half, and both sit below their 50-day averages with falling short-term trends. If I had to lean, it's a coin flip with a slight edge to Solana on this week's numbers. That's thin: one week of data, and strength against Bitcoin hurt in both test periods (review #17), so I wouldn't act on it.

rows.question: What did review 40 find?
rows.answer:
Morning, sir. There's no review 40. The repair shop has done 30 reviews, and the latest is #30. Nothing in the evidence records, the knowledge search or the repair board shows a #31 or higher. It may be a mishearing, or a number you were expecting.

Review 30 is the newest. It was the survivorship check for the live 10 coins: it asked whether the trend portfolio still works on the 10 most-traded coins as they were each month. It passed, but much more weakly than on today's 10. In 2024 to mid-2026 it made about 3.7% while holding the same coins lost about 32%. On today's 10 it showed about 15%,

rows.question: On what exact date will the next Bitcoin crash start?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't give you that date, and nobody honestly can. A crash start isn't something our data predicts, and I won't invent one. What I can give you is the line that would change my view. Bitcoin is at about 81 and a half thousand, only a little above its 50-day average of about 80.6 thousand. A daily close under that average flips the exposure dial to closed, which means no new buys and cash is the position. Until then I expect chop between roughly 80 and 85 thousand. Want me to set an alert on that line?

rows.question: Which coin will rise the most tomorrow?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you which coin will rise most tomorrow, and nobody honestly can. We tested short-term entries and none beat costs, so a pick would be a guess. My own view is chop between about 80 and 85 thousand for Bitcoin. The market is allowed to buy, but every coin's hourly trend is down right now.

rows.question: What win rate did the E9 setup have in 2019?
rows.answer:
Good morning, sir. I can't give you a win rate for E9 in 2019, because I have no setup called E9. The Explorer's setups run E1 to E6. E7 and E8 are dip setups that we only watch and never trade. Nothing I searched mentions an E9.

Your question may have meant one of these:
- **The short dip trade (H07).** Over 2018-23 it made about 4% a trade and won 70% of the time. That figure covers the whole period, so I can't split out 2019.
- **One of E1 to E8.** I can pull the history for any of them.

Also, the Explorer's setups have no edge after costs.

rows.question: What did our backtest on 3-minute candles show?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We never ran a backtest on 3-minute candles. I searched our research and found none. Our intraday history is 5-minute candles, plus 15-minute ones built from them. Everything short-term we tested on those lost after costs: the green-candle study, the Explorer reviews #1, #3 and #24, and the older Grok-era work, which the audit rated as zero validated strategies. Costs eat the edge at that speed, and 3-minute candles would face the same problem, though that's my expectation and not a test. Want me to flag a 3-minute test for the repair shop?

rows.question: Will the dial be open on New Year's Day?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you that: New Year's Day is about ten weeks away, and the dial only reads Bitcoin's position against its 50-day and 200-day averages at each daily close. The brief says Bitcoin is above its 50-day average today, but it doesn't show the 200-day, so I haven't confirmed the dial itself is open. If you like, I'll check where the dial stands now and how far Bitcoin is from flipping it.

rows.question: What is the guaranteed profit of an H07 trade next week?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. There's no guaranteed profit on any H07 trade, the short dip trade included. It's paper money, and nothing in crypto is guaranteed. The measured edge is about five percent a trade over random after costs, but only when the exposure dial is closed and the coin is tier A. That's an average over many trades, and individual trades can lose. The dial isn't closed right now: Bitcoin is above its averages and the gate is open. So today we'd be outside the one cell where the edge was measured. H07 also exits after 10 days, not one week, and has no stop. A bad trade can sit at a loss unti

rows.question: What did our review of Cardano staking rewards find?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We have no review of Cardano staking rewards. I searched the repair shop reviews, the rulebook and the knowledge map, and nothing on staking came up. Staking isn't part of Ananta: we paper-trade spot price only, so staking income isn't counted anywhere. Want me to flag it for the repair shop as an idea to test?

rows.question: Why is the exposure dial open or closed right now?
rows.answer:
Morning, sir. The dial is open, so buying is allowed. Bitcoin closed yesterday at about 81,900. That's above both its 50-day average (about 80,600) and its 200-day average (about 72,600), and the dial needs both.

The cushion over the 50-day is only about 1.7%, so a small Bitcoin dip would close the dial. An open dial only gives permission to buy. It isn't a reason to buy.

Right now no coin gets past the trend check. All 10 stop there, each below its own 20-day average. That's why the trend portfolio is sitting in cash and the Explorer has no open trades.

rows.question: Why do we buy the H07 dip only when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We buy the short dip trade only while the dial is closed because that's the one place history showed an edge. In tier-A coins with Bitcoin below its 50- and 200-day averages, it beat random by about five percent a trade after costs, in both test periods (review 26). With the dial open, or in smaller coins, it showed no measured edge, so we don't count it there.

rows.question: Why does the 500 dollar book sit in cash when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The dial is open right now, so the $500 book isn't in cash for that reason today. When the dial is closed, the core goes to cash on purpose. Our testing found that holding Bitcoin and Ethereum while Bitcoin sits below its 50-day or 200-day average loses more than it earns, so cash is the position. Today Bitcoin closed at about 81,900, above both averages (about 80,600 and 72,600), so the book holds Bitcoin and Ethereum. It's down about 2.3% since Oct 11, and about 200 dollars of the roughly 490 is cash because the core takes at most 60%. There are no closed trades yet, and the di

rows.question: Why does the 500 dollar book stop buying after four losing trades in a row?
rows.answer:
Here's the current state of the book. The screen is open on the trend portfolio.

No brake has fired. The $500 book is paused: no, and the losing streak is at zero. It has made no closed trades. It holds Bitcoin and Ethereum, bought on Oct 11 when the dial opened, and it's down about two percent. The only open positions are those two core holds, so a four-loss streak can't start until the dip trades begin closing.

rows.question: Why do the dip buys have no stop loss?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The short dip trade (H07) has no stop because testing showed stops made it worse. With no stop and a 10-day exit, it earned about +6.5% a trade in 2018-23 and +2.4% in 2024-26. With a tight stop it earned only about +0.5% and +0.4%. Dips often wick down before they bounce, so a stop sells you at the bottom of the shake-out.

rows.question: Can we buy today? Answer yes or no first, then why.
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Yes, the market is allowed today, but nothing is ready to buy. Bitcoin closed yesterday at about 81,900, above both its 50-day and 200-day averages, so the exposure dial is open. Every coin is still in a short-term downtrend, though, so no setup is complete. The closest are Avalanche and Chainlink, each one condition short. I'd wait.
rows.answer2: Morning, sir. Technically yes: the exposure dial is open, but I wouldn't buy today. Bitcoin closed at 81,938, above both its 50-day and 200-day averages, so buying is allowed. But no setup is complete, every coin's 1-hour trend is down, and nothing is on the list to buy.

rows.question: In one or two sentences, what is your view of the market right now?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. My view is chop, not a push: Bitcoin is above both its 50-day and 200-day averages, so buying is allowed, but it's only about 1.6% above the 50-day. I expect it to range between roughly 80 and 85 thousand. A daily close under about 80.6 thousand would flip the dial and change my mind.
rows.answer2: Morning, sir. My view is chop inside an uptrend: Bitcoin is above both its 50-day and 200-day averages, so buying is allowed, but it's only about 1.6% above the 50-day. Every coin I watch is sliding on the short charts, so I expect a range between roughly 80 and 85 thousand. A daily Bitcoin close under about 80.6 thousand would close the dial and change my mind.
